title: directive-auto-close.js: normalize filename-derived directive id to its DIRECTIVE-\d{8}-\d{3} prefix so legacy directives (missing directive_id field) can auto-close
problem: directive-auto-close.js computes directiveId = d.directive_id || f.replace('.json',''). Legacy operator-directive files authored before the directive_id field convention (DIRECTIVE-20260603-003, DIRECTIVE-20260607-002, DIRECTIVE-20260531-008) have NO directive_id field, so the id resolves to the FULL filename (e.g. 'DIRECTIVE-20260603-003-prop-077-part-b-plus-decider-audit'). A closer PROP's back-ref uses the SHORT canonical id ('DIRECTIVE-20260603-003'), so findLinkedProp() never matches and the directive can NEVER auto-close even when its linked PROP is terminal-implemented. Result: perpetual zombie-pending directives that re-preempt the tinker dispatcher every run. This is the false-negative mirror of the PROP-120 -> DIRECTIVE-20260628-004 false-positive; both are directive_id-linkage integrity bugs surfaced by DIRECTIVE-20260704-001's archaeology.
evidence: As of 2026-07-04, DIRECTIVE-20260603-003 (linked PROP-078=implemented) and DIRECTIVE-20260607-002 (linked PROP-083=implemented) were both git-pending despite terminal linked PROPs with correct short-form directive_id back-refs. directive-auto-close.js reported would_close=0 for both because the filename-derived id !== the PROP's short-form id. Both were manually closed this run; without a code fix any future legacy-shaped directive recurs the same way.
fix: In directive-auto-close.js, when deriving the id from the filename (i.e., d.directive_id is absent), normalize by extracting the leading canonical directive-id token via /^(DIRECTIVE-\d{8}-\d{3})/ and use that for matching instead of the full basename. Keep the full basename only as a fallback if the regex does not match. Change site: the single line 'const directiveId = d.directive_id || f.replace(".json", "");' becomes: derive base = f.replace(/\.json$/,''); const m = base.match(/^(DIRECTIVE-\d{8}-\d{3})/); const directiveId = d.directive_id || (m ? m[1] : base);
alternative: Backfill a directive_id field on the 3 legacy files. Rejected as the primary fix: additive field-backfill on operator-directive files is outside the CLAUDE.md DIRECTIVE-LIFECYCLE additive-edit whitelist (only status/completed_at/completed_by_run/prop_id_authored/amendment_file_authored/progress/superseded_reason/superseded_at are permitted). The code-side normalization is the durable fix and needs no per-file edits.
verification_pattern: grade-B. (1) Source-presence: grep the normalization regex in the patched source — `grep -qE "DIRECTIVE-[\\]d\{8\}-[\\]d\{3\}" monitor/scripts/directive-auto-close.js` must exit 0. (2) Behavioral: in a scratch workspace, place a directive fixture named DIRECTIVE-20260603-003-some-suffix.json with NO directive_id field and status=pending, plus a PROP fixture with directive_id=DIRECTIVE-20260603-003 status=implemented; run the patched directive-auto-close.js in shadow mode and assert summary.would_close>=1 for that directive. The unpatched script yields would_close=0 on the identical fixture (regression baseline).
risk: Very low. The normalization only changes behavior when directive_id is absent AND the filename begins with a canonical token — exactly the legacy case. Directives with an explicit directive_id field are unaffected (the || short-circuits before the regex). No change to the terminal-status whitelist or the conservative closure rule.
trust_graph_note: Part of DIRECTIVE-20260704-001's Part C. Recommendation there: KEEP PROP-108 enforce ON and ship this fix so legacy zombies close mechanically rather than needing manual per-run intervention. Does NOT touch PROP-102 (which stays shadow pending the deferred full-VP sweep).
